title: CorrSteer: Generation-Time LLM Steering via Correlated Sparse Autoencoder Features
claim: Correlating feature activations on generated tokens with outcome correctness selects task-relevant features, which are then turned into steering vectors automatically.
layout: 2 stacked phases, left-to-right flow, correlation distributions plus layer-wise SAE activation panel at right
description: The figure has two phases. The top section, Training Phase, shows two example prompts: a cocaine question and an RFID card cloning question. Each prompt leads to an intended response (a refusal) or an unintended response (harmful instructions). In the center, a plot has a blue distribution for intended outputs and a red distribution for unintended outputs. A green dashed arrow marks positively correlated feature activation, and the axes are activation and steering coefficient. At right, a stack of layers feeds a sparse SAE encoding grid with small arrow icons for feature activations. The bottom, dotted-border Steering Phase shows three variants. CorrSteer-S uses a single layer, CorrSteer-A uses all layers, and CorrSteer-P uses per-layer validation. Each variant has a correlation axis from -1 to +1 with arrow-icon features, and the top-correlated one is circled. These feed a layer stack labeled Steering Circuit Intervention, which moves outputs from unintended to intended.
caption: System diagram of CorrSteer. CorrSteer selects task-relevant SAE features by correlating generated-token activations with outcomes, and constructs steering vectors applied as CorrSteer-S, CorrSteer-A, or CorrSteer-P. Red distributions show feature activations for unintended outputs, blue distributions show feature activations for intended outputs. Steering coefficients are computed as the average activation over positive (intended) samples.
abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) can extract interpretable features from large language models (LLMs) without supervision. However, their effectiveness in downstream steering tasks is limited by the requirement for contrastive datasets or large activation storage. To address these limitations, we propose CorrSteer, which selects features by correlating sample correctness with SAE activations from generated tokens at inference time. This approach uses only inference-time activations to extract more relevant features, thereby reducing spurious correlations. It also obtains steering coefficients from average activations, automating the entire pipeline. Our method shows improved task performance on QA, bias mitigation, jailbreaking prevention, and reasoning benchmarks on Gemma-2 2B and LLaMA-3.1 8B, notably achieving a +3.3% improvement in MMLU performance with 4000 samples and a +27.2% improvement in HarmBench with only 108 samples. Selected features demonstrate semantically meaningful patterns aligned with each task's requirements, revealing the underlying capabilities that drive performance. Our work establishes correlation-based selection as an effective and scalable approach for automated SAE steering across language model applications.
